caption:
Is 16 CFR part 1307 on your kids' product certificate?
Under 16 CFR 1307.3, children's toys and child care articles can't be made for sale, offered for sale, distributed or imported with more than 0.1 percent of eight listed phthalates, including DEHP, DBP and DINP.
It applies to plasticized component parts too, like soft vinyl.
Run your product through the Finder to see which rules apply.

sources.claim: Eight phthalates over 0.1% prohibited in children's toys and child care articles, incl. plasticized parts
sources.quote: (a) ... the manufacture for sale, offer for sale, distribution in commerce, or importation into the United States of any children's toy or child care article that contains concentrations of more than 0.1 percent of di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) , dibutyl phthalate (DBP), or benzyl butyl phthalate (BBP) is prohibited. (b) ... more than 0.1 percent of diisononyl phthalate (DINP), diisobutyl phthalate (DIBP), di- n -pentyl phthalate (DPENP), di- n -hexyl phthalate (DHEXP), or dicyclohexyl phthalate (DCHP) is prohibited. (c) ... the restrictions stated in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section apply to any plasticized component part of a children's toy or child care article
Children's toy means a consumer product designed or intended by the manufacturer for a child 12 years of age or younger for use by the child when the child plays.
Finished product certificates must identify separately all applicable rules, bans, standards, or regulations.
